explanation.text: The Logic: Information Ratio = (Portfolio Return – Benchmark Return) / Tracking Error, where tracking error is the standard deviation of the active return (Rp – Rb). It measures how much active return a manager generates per unit of active risk taken, making it the standard benchmark-relative measure of consistent alpha. The Trap: '(Rp – Rf)/sigma' is the Sharpe Ratio (excess return over the risk-free rate divided by total volatility). 'Rp/beta' has no standard interpretation. 'Rf/sigma' is not a recognised performance ratio. Note: The Information Ratio formula is not in the cited NISM Series XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook pages checked; it is supported in the fallback Series XXI-B workbook (Portfolio Managers, pages 376–377), which defines IR as (Rp – Rb)/Stdev(p – b). The framing above is presented as general performance-measurement knowledge rather than as a XXI-A workbook citation.
